item.title: Switzerland Confirms AI-Assisted Cyberattacks Breached Critical Infrastructure Operators
item.description: Attackers using AI agents have broken into computer systems at Swiss organizations in four of five confirmed attacks, the first such cases in the country, the country's cybersecurity agency said yesterday. Three of the attacks targeted critical infrastructure operators, and two of those succeeded, with no major disruptions reported. The victims have not been named, and it is not known who is behind the attacks. Florian Schütz , who directs Switzerland's National Cyber Security Centre, gave the figures in an interview with public broadcaster SRF. All five cases were reported in recent days. Small and medium-sized companies were among the organizations hit, and they came forward voluntarily. The agency's first notice, a security advisory published on Tuesday, said the agents had compromised the victims' IT systems in every case known at that point. Neither the notice nor yesterday's broadcast interview explains why the count changed. "These cases re...

item.title: Unpatched Cacti Zero-Day Enables RCE in Just Four HTTP Requests via Guest Access
item.description: Details have emerged about a new zero-day vulnerability in Cacti , an open-source network monitoring tool, that could be exploited to achieve remote code execution. The proof-of-concept (PoC) exploit, which has yet to be assigned a CVE identifier, has been tracked as 4HTTP2SHELL and 4HTTP2ROOT . "I found a path from a fresh, unauthenticated HTTP session to command execution as the Cacti server user in four requests," a security researcher who goes by the online alias "ek0ms savi0r" said . "No login. No valid API key. No phishing. Just four HTTP requests against the default guest surface." The shortcoming affects Cacti Core 1.2.31, the latest version , on an isolated host when the guest account is enabled. At a high level, the vulnerability allows an attacker to abuse the guest access to write an unvalidated value (i.e., non-numeric text) into a setting called "preview_graphs_per_page" via "auth_profile.php?action=update_data."...

item.title: ThreatsDay: 10M NGINX Services at Risk, 250+ Malicious Extensions, AI Server Hijacking + 17 More Stories
item.description: A website can look perfectly fine to the person running it. Log out, visit the same page, and things might look different. Something similar is happening with browser extensions, where even the way you find and install one can change what it does. Checking whether software works as expected only tells you so much. Then there’s the question of who gets to use what. Stolen logins are opening doors across connected systems, while some AI servers are sitting online for anyone to use at someone else’s expense. Even software responsible for keeping the power on has found its way into an attack. Meanwhile, authorities are taking down large scam operations, extortion gangs are making comebacks, and ransomware activity is picking up. Some of the more worrying findings this week involve things most people would have little reason to suspect. The details are worth a look. The threats change every week. Subscribe, and we’ll alert you when each new ThreatsDay Bulletin is out.

item.title: North Korea-Linked PolinRider Poisons Over 7,600 GitHub Repositories to Spread Malware
item.description: The threat actors behind the PolinRider campaign have been observed planting a Python loader in GitHub repositories, as evidence emerges that the activity may have started as far back as February 2025. "The loader hides in a small utils package or in conftest.py," SafeDep said in a report published this week. "When Python imports the file, the loader reads the newest transaction that an Ethereum wallet sent to itself. It decodes the input data of that transaction as JavaScript and runs it with Node.js." The JavaScript code, for its part, reads a second wallet to locate the command-and-control (C2) server and then passes the next stage to a detached interactive Node.js environment by means of a node -i process. The software supply chain security company said it identified the loader in 375 public repositories that belong to 260 accounts. There is no evidence that the loader has been distributed via PyPI or npm. PolinRider is the name assigned to a mali...

item.title: Most Wanted: The Phishing Kits and Techniques Getting Past Security Controls
item.description: Every phishing attack has to get past email security, web filtering, and safe browsing before it reaches an employee. Some kits manage that far more often than others, and those are the kits that security teams need to know about. At Push Security, we measure this as breakthrough rate : The share of attacks that get past email security, web gateways, and safe browsing to reach the user. How an attack breaks through Every browser-based attack starts with a lure, and each control in its path sees only part of the attack: Email security: Half of the attacks we see never touch email. The lure arrives through a search ad, a chat message, social media, a calendar invite, or a QR code. The rest come from trusted senders and services, so they pass reputation checks. Web gateways: The pages sit on trusted hosting and are assembled in the browser. The domains rotate every few days, so reputation data lags behind them. item.description: Drupal has warned of a new "highly critical" security flaw impacting Drupal core that it said has been exploited in the wild. The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-136716 (CVSS score: N/A), has been described as a case of improper checking for unusual or exceptional conditions. "However, certain sites in unusual or incomplete install states remain vulnerable to site takeover following that advisory, including production sites."
